message: Imported canonical English Task 2 fixture Context 'advisor1/style' into profile 'task-2-proposal-authority'.

33503d41-7b99-5526-a028-0a1a20652c0d.content: Avoid em dashes in the proposal; split the sentence or use more ordinary punctuation instead.

79437c17-1f08-5188-8177-c622429dc4f9.content: The user tends to place several independently reviewable claims in one long sentence.

807a906c-d519-59b1-8406-43c8015ef068.content: Use first-person active voice for choices and commitments owned by the proposal author so responsibility remains explicit throughout the work plan.

e463a3b5-263f-58da-9895-242965892e60.content: Describe prototype operations that have already been implemented and verified as observed states.

fef78af8-1774-5da0-8345-571eb8c9cc3c.content: Describe prototype operations not yet implemented or evaluated as plans or expectations.

ff8f0b12-9df4-5968-90b2-cd8d971dcc1b.content: When a commitment is phrased passively, readers may interpret it as uncertainty, evasiveness, or reluctance to take responsibility.

6c282ef7-4326-5d69-a7c4-d3f4f3a3a508.content: Use “we” only for decisions and commitments the authors control, not for external facts or actions owned by another party.

58565355-bec5-5b2b-89ed-f0b8cab0351a.content: The user should use one first-person pronoun consistently for the same authorial role and should not alternate between “I” and “we” unless the responsible party actually changes.

bec16e02-b267-50b8-9c0e-964184f2a6b4.content: The user tends to hide unsettled commitments behind passive phrases such as “will be considered” or “is expected.”

cc860653-ad91-52f8-91db-5b26371dca0a.content: Split proposal prose into short sentences when a sentence contains more than one independently reviewable claim.

af0d191d-d23e-562b-997b-b1024dacefda.content: Keep one main claim in each sentence so a reviewer can locate and assess it quickly.

13dc50e1-ecaa-504e-a602-7a10a09d5484.content: The user tends to repeat em dashes when a sentence already contains several clauses.

358230d3-9ff0-51b9-9bf6-0752a2d9845a.content: Repeated em dashes can shift a reviewer’s attention from the proposal’s argument to suspicion that its prose was generated by AI.
